items.reason: GM-CSF and cyclophosphamide are given as adjuncts to the ERC1671 tumour cell/lysate vaccine ("ERC1671 in combination with GM-CSF and cyclophosphamide"; cyclophosphamide "used for immunopotentiation"), with no own antitumour outcome; pembrolizumab is the only pharmacological agent tested as an antitumour agent.

Stated purpose is immune modulation for the vaccine: "used for immunopotentiation ... as an antineoplastic and immunosuppressant agent to modulate immunity". This is the vaccine-support analogue of R6 conditioning chemotherapy; no antitumour outcome is attributed to it. R4 does not list cyclophosphamide explicitly, so XL may prefer to code it as part of the excluded vaccine therapy instead; either way it is not a candidate.

With GM-CSF and cyclophosphamide as vaccine adjuncts, bevacizumab as backbone and the vaccine an excluded type, pembrolizumab is the only investigational pharmacological agent (cf. worked example 'Pembrolizumab + an investigational vaccine').
